answer: I'd like to talk about my younger sister, who is probably the most hard-working person I know. A time I felt enormously proud of a family member was when she finished at the top of her year in her HSC exams and received an award at her college's prize-giving ceremony last year. I had watched her study relentlessly for two years, often sacrificing her social life, so her success felt thoroughly [[well-deserved]]. The whole family went to the ceremony, and my parents were dressed in their best clothes. In our family, education has always been treated as something precious, so this meant a great deal to my parents. Sitting in the audience, I felt [[a lump in my throat]] as her name was called out for the special award. It was a genuinely [[emotional]] moment for the whole family, and my mother could not stop wiping her eyes. What made me so proud was not just the achievement itself, but the [[perseverance]] and discipline she had shown to get there. I remembered all the times she had doubted herself and kept going anyway, sometimes studying until two in the morning. Honestly, seeing her hard work pay off so publicly was one of the most [[uplifting]] experiences I have had. Afterwards, we went out for sweets and tea, and she could not stop smiling. I told her how proud I was, and I meant every word. It was a powerful reminder that dedication truly does pay off in the end, and it made me want to push myself harder too.

followUps.q: Do you and your sister get on well?
followUps.answer: Very well. We tease each other constantly, as siblings do, but she is also the person I talk to when something is bothering me. She gives surprisingly wise advice for her age.

followUps.q: How did your family celebrate her success?
followUps.answer: We had a special dinner at home, and my mother cooked all her favourite dishes. My father also phoned my grandparents in the village, who were absolutely delighted to hear the news.

note: Persona fix: sister is still a student, so 'graduated' became an HSC top result and college award; 'deserved' -> 'well-deserved'; marked 'a lump in my throat'.
